text:
Florian Xhekaj's opportunity arrived through someone else's injury. With Chris Kreider out 6 to 8 weeks, as The Sick Podcast reported, the 22 year old drew into Montreal's lineup, and The Hockey News called it a "Prime Opportunity For Florian Xhekaj."

He has 3 points in 9 games on under 8 minutes a night, plus 26 hits, which tells you how he plays. In that small sample, the Canadiens have held 62% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five. Nine games of fourth line minutes is a tiny sample, so treat it as a good first impression, not a verdict.

Reporters are watching the details. Andrew Berkshire of Game Over Network wrote that "Florian Xhekaj's awareness without the puck could use some work," and Karine Hains of The Hockey News noted he went into one game not knowing who he'd play with.

A fourth round pick in 2023 and the younger brother of Arber Xhekaj, he scored 24 goals in 69 AHL games for Laval in 2024-25. The finishing touch is real at that level, and Kreider's absence opens a longer look.
